ratings.note: Directly matches a mostly downstream event stream.
Client messages need a separate HTTP request path.
EventSource defines reconnect behavior and supports event IDs.
Framed messages can carry the same status updates.
The same connection supports frequent client messages.
The application must define reconnect, resubscribe, and replay behavior.

modeData.decisionRule: Prefer SSE when updates are mostly downstream and its HTTP path fits the infrastructure; choose WebSocket when a durable bidirectional session is part of the product need.

title: SSE or WebSocket for a status stream?
summary: Trace the same reconnecting status client through two transport choices and choose by interaction shape.

truthLadder.analogy: SSE is like a live radio station from server to listener; WebSocket is more like an open phone call where either side can speak.
truthLadder.technical: EventSource receives server-sent events over HTTP with defined reconnect behavior, while WebSocket establishes a bidirectional framed protocol after its opening handshake.
truthLadder.caveat: Proxies, authentication, browser limits, backpressure, infrastructure, and library behavior can outweigh the protocol-level distinction.

teachBack.question: Which option is the default fit for mostly server-to-client status updates?
teachBack.answer: SSE is often the simpler fit when HTTP streaming and its reconnect model meet the infrastructure and product constraints.

teachBack.question: When does WebSocket earn its added application lifecycle work?
teachBack.answer: When frequent low-latency messages must flow in both directions or the product already needs a bidirectional session.
